decisions_recorded: A week crossing 1 January is split into two rows (one per calendar year), so every row has one year and one FEC cycle and the year sums reconcile to 08 exactly; sum by study_sector x chamber x week_start for whole weeks.
weekly_giving is the complete covered week grid (zero rows are counted zeros); 2026 is covered through each index's max transaction date, equal to 08's note.
dem_share = d/(d+r) on net dollars (brief and 08); dem_share_gross on gross positive dollars (the Codex contract's primary outcome) alongside.
Channel by funding_source: employee_original -> employee; pac_activity -> company_pac; everything else -> other_included_receipt; transfer_receipt gross shown separately.
Committee sheets keyed by 08's per-row party (no committee-cycle has more than one party).
Donor keys are hashed (16 hex of SHA-256); no donor names in the workbook.

expected_dem_net_gain = expected D seats - D seats at the start of the outgoing Congress (seat_results.csv, the previous election as seated), fixed within cycle; the files' own net changes kept alongside (three Crystal Ball rows measured from another baseline: House 2004, House 2006, Senate 2018).
Toss-ups split evenly (ratings snapshots; the two unassigned Georgia seats of the 2020 Senate call); Crystal Ball rows with no projected seats have blank expected seats.

backfilled = run date after forecastdate (includes the two launch-day rows with a 1-day lag); availability unverified (2018 538, undated Crystal Ball finals) -> aligned_sensitivity only; the undated Crystal Ball sensitivity date is election day (the latest a final pre-election call can be).

Among forecasts available before week_start, the latest by forecast_date is taken (not the latest run time): a backfill batch releases many old dates at once and the most recent information is the latest-dated one.
Same election cycle = the row's FEC cycle; election and post-election weeks kept in aligned, flagged (week_position, primary_window).
Crystal Ball dates parsed only where the file records one (quote text or the ljsYYYYMMDD article slug).
538 run timestamps carry no time zone; used as recorded; availability compared by calendar date (a run after midnight Monday is not available to that week).
gaps_and_risks: Only cycle 2022 has complete pre-election weeks paired after the gate (18 per 538 version per chamber). 2024: Crystal Ball finals dated 2024-11-04, no week_start before election day after that date. 2026: snapshots dated after the last indexed transaction. 2020: money not collected yet; after the 2020 rerun at most 3 House weeks (Oct 12, 19, 26) and 6 Senate weeks (Sep 21 - Oct 26) can pair with 538.
538's House/Senate fundamentals include a Fundraising component (2020 README): a feedback path from money to the Classic/Deluxe forecasts; per-version weights not held locally.

CAND_ICI is the FEC's code in cn files downloaded 2026-09-08 (end-of-cycle status), not a status fixed at a forecast origin; 9 linked candidate rows are absent from the same-cycle cn file; 13 have a blank CAND_ICI.
company_pac channel here is only the index's recipient-side PAC activity ($139,000 House/Senate); the FEC pas2 company-PAC-to-candidate channel is not in 08's population.
Donor keys are not certified person identities (Mentat's identity_basis); 4.31% of House/Senate gross dollars carry the reported NAME|STATE|ZIP fallback key.
Committee sheets have no zero-receipt candidates (the index holds only money that exists); a contemporaneous all-candidate universe needs the full FEC candidate files.
rerun_for_2020: after 08 is re-linked with 2019-2020 (new population pin(s), committee_map rows for 2019-2020, fec_cn20 in its sources): python build_09.py, then verify_09.py on the stage, install and a new receipt; the builder reads years, pins, committee map and cn files from 08 at run time and fails closed if 08 and the indexes disagree. A multi-pin (union) population is de-duplicated by facts.source_id; verify_09.py flags multi-pin populations for an update before it can pass.
